rules.infinite_in_degree: X_1(37) has a function of degree 18 over Q (its gonality), hence infinitely many points of degree 18 by Hilbert irreducibility
rules.sporadic: not sporadic: X_1(37) has a function of degree 18 over Q (its gonality), hence infinitely many points of degree 18 by Hilbert irreducibility
rules.isolated: dim L(x) = 1 (P^1-isolated, verified here); AV-isolated by Theorem 48 of the appendix by Derickx and van Hoeij to Bourdon-Hashimoto-Keller-Klagsbrun-Lowry-Duda-Morrison-Najman-Shukla (formal immersion through X_1(37) -> X_0(37) -> X_0^+(37))

points.reference: A. Bourdon, S. Hashimoto, T. Keller, Z. Klagsbrun, D. Lowry-Duda, T. Morrison, F. Najman, H. Shukla, Towards a classification of isolated j-invariants, Math. Comp. 94 (2025), 447-473, arXiv:2311.07740 (with an appendix by M. Derickx and M. van Hoeij); see also A. Bourdon, O. Ejder, Rational isolated j-invariants from X_1(l^n) and X_0(l^n), arXiv:2506.19560, Theorem 4. The point itself (degree 18, not sporadic since gon_Q X_1(37) = 18) is noted in Bourdon-Ejder-Liu-Odumodu-Viray, Adv. Math. 357 (2019), proof of Theorem 8.1, and in Sutherland's 2012 notes.
